title: Iulii Firmici Iunioris Mathesis
shelf_note: A 15th-century humanist-cursive manuscript of Firmicus Maternus' Mathesis (Latin astrology), as catalogued. There is no tradition and no collection to test it against.
structure_note: The image is one leaf AFTER the text it carries (see page 218). That may be a book-wide offset, which one page cannot settle. printed_backsteps 49 and printed_repeats 46 against 169 printed numbers look like misread furniture, not a real disorder: this page's <page-num>VI comes from the running book number 'VI' at the head of the leaf, which repeats on every leaf of Book VI. The real foliation is the pencil '107' at the foot. pages_translated is 0 in the structure counts but the field says 302, so one of the two instruments is wrong.

pages.printed_marker: "VI" (faint, head of leaf, book number); "107" (pencil, foot right)
pages.layout: single column of humanist cursive; red rubric line and red marginal headings in the outer margin ("Natale pyndari et Archilochi poete lyrici", "pro imperiis"); two-line initial S's; show-through from the verso

ocr_errors.ocr: sibi aspiciat: nec sint alia partium societate coniuncti … hec genitura diuinam et celestem
ocr_errors.image: The leaf opens "[con]stitutionum reddit interpretem q[ui] doct[is] sermone et diuini ingenii potestate compositus celesti quodammodo institutione formatus … Hec genitura platonis fuisse suggeritur", then the nativities of Pindar and Archilochus and of Archimedes, the rubric "Quid faciant stelle in diversis locis vel finibus collocate. Et primo de Saturno in Libra", and Saturn in Libra
ocr_errors.problem: The transcription is the text of the PRECEDING leaf (the poverty and blindness configurations, Demosthenes, Homer, and the opening of Plato). Its last words, "diuinam et celestem", run on into this image's first line. None of the OCR text is on this image.

ocr_errors.image: "VI" at the head of the leaf is the running book number; the leaf's folio is the pencil "107"
ocr_errors.problem: The book number was taken as the page number

book_verdict: The scan is one leaf ahead of its text. A reader sees Plato, Pindar and Archimedes on the image while the text and English give Demosthenes and Homer from the leaf before. The translation of that text is reasonably faithful, but it smooths corrupt lines, and two notes explain misreads by guessing.
